# Issue tracker: GitHub Issues

Issues and specs for this repo live in GitHub Issues of the **base repository** (the
`upstream` remote in the fork model, else `origin`). Use the `gh` CLI; it is authenticated on
this machine.

## Conventions

- **Branches and commits** carry the issue as `GH-<n>`: branch `GH-<n>-Short-Title`,
  commit subject `GH-<n> type(scope): …` (see `hassan-devkit commits:show`). A leading
  `#<n>` is never used in a subject — git treats `#` lines as comments in the editor.
- **PR body** ends with `Closes #<n>` so the issue closes on merge.
- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --repo <owner/repo> --title … --body …`.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <n> --comments`.
- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open` (add `--label` / `--assignee @me` as needed).
- **Comment**: `gh issue comment <n> --body …`.
- **Assign — always to the current user when you start an issue**: whoever starts the work
  owns it. `hassan-devkit worktree:create GH-<n>-…` runs `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`
  for the branch's issue; for any other way of picking up an issue, run that yourself first.
  There is no status field: an open PR is the progress signal.
- **Labels**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-label … / --remove-label …`.
- **Close**: `gh issue close <n>` (or let the PR's `Closes #<n>` do it).

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a GitHub issue on the base repository.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Fetch the issue with its comments (`gh issue view <n> --comments`).

## Wayfinding operations

The **map** is a single issue labelled `wayfinder-map`; child issues carry a `Part of #<map>`
line at the top of the body and a `wayfinder-<type>` label (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`).
Blocking is a `Blocked by #<n>` line in the body (GitHub has no native blocking link outside
Projects). Claim = assign to yourself; resolve = comment with the answer, then close.
